geometry._trackwidth_note: trackwidth is the CALIPER-MEASURED wheel separation (stakeholder, 128 mm). Do NOT bend it to make turns land -- it is the one independently verifiable number in this file. Scrub correction belongs in calibration.rotational_slip; main.cpp derives an effective track = trackwidth / rotational_slip and hands THAT to Drive/Odometry/plannerLimits.

calibration._otos_linear_scale_note: 2026-07-30 (126-003), camera-measured on the playfield, robot tethered. 18 straight-line runs (lengths 150/300/350mm, both directions, 3 reps each, ping-ponged to stay field-safe), OTOS delta (already scaled by the then-committed 1.067) vs. camera-measured travel at rest before/after each leg. Fit OTOS_mm = slope * camera_mm through the origin: slope=1.0384 (OTOS reads consistently long). Residual against the OLD 1.067 value: mean +3.91% sd 0.79% (95% CI [+3.55%,+4.27%], n=18) -- excludes 0, so 1.067 was wrong, not just noisy. Corrected = old_committed x (1/slope) = 1.067 x 0.9630 = 1.0275. A prior 12-run pilot set (lengths 150/300mm only, before repositioning for the 350mm block) gave a consistent 1.0330 -- both land in the same ~1.03 neighborhood, not the committed 1.067. Reflashed (mbdeploy, gen_boot_config.py regenerated boot_config.cpp's linearScale=1.0275f) and re-verified with a 6-run post-reflash spot-check (300mm, both directions, 3 reps): residual collapsed to mean +0.37% sd 0.34% (95% CI [+0.10%,+0.65%], n=6) -- an order of magnitude tighter than the pre-correction +3.91%, though still technically nonzero at this sample's precision (implied further correction ~1.0236, ~1mm on a 290mm leg). Not chasing that last fraction of a percent further -- it is at or below the camera measurement's own noise floor (a few mm of AprilTag pose jitter) and well past the point of diminishing returns for a boot-baked constant. Provenance of the original 1.067 is unknown (predates this sprint); this is the first camera-anchored measurement of it.
calibration._rotational_slip_note: 2026-07-29, camera-measured on the playfield. Scrub: the ratio of ACTUAL rotation to what ideal differential kinematics (omega = (vR-vL)/b) predict -- a skid-steer robot drags its wheels sideways through a turn and under-rotates. 180 deg in-place turns vs overhead AprilTag truth, 3 W->N->E / 3 E->N->W: 180.3 deg actual (sd 1.9), 100.2%. Equivalent to an effective track of 140.4 mm against the measured 128. Domain {0} u [0.5, 1.0] (config.proto); 0 is the uncalibrated sentinel meaning apply no correction. Consumed at BOOT (gen_boot_config.py -> boot_config.cpp -> main.cpp kEffectiveTrack); a runtime CONFIG rotSlip patch acks ERR_UNIMPLEMENTED, so changing it needs a reflash.
calibration._rotation_calibration_note: 2026-07-29, camera-measured, robot untethered. Turn response is affine: actual = gain*commanded + offset, fitted over 48 shuffled in-place turns (15/30/45/90/135/180 deg, both directions, omega 2.5/4.5/6.5/8.0 rad/s). The SAME law holds at every rate -- accuracy does not degrade with speed, so this is geometry/stiction, not a dynamics artifact. The ~-6 deg offset is why small turns were so bad: a 15 deg command landed at 9. Inverting it (commanded = (desired - offset)/gain) and re-running 47 trials gave a residual of mean +0.64 deg, sd 2.13, max 6.5 -- verified at 8.0 rad/s as well as 2.5. SIGN MAPPING, confirm before trusting: these were measured in the camera frame, where POSITIVE commanded omega DECREASES yaw. _pos here = positive commanded omega (clockwise in camera), _neg = negative. NOT YET CONSUMED BY FIRMWARE: rotation_gain_pos/neg and rotation_offset/neg exist in msg::DrivetrainConfig but have no reader and no emitter in gen_boot_config.py -- dead data, exactly as rotational_slip was before this session. Compensation is currently applied host-side (scratchpad turn_verify.py) because the robot is on battery and cannot be reflashed; wire it up next time it is on the bench.

control._vel_gains_note: 2026-07-15 RESONANCE TAMED (106-002, live config() gain sweep -- P4 binary wire, tests/bench/velocity_step_response.py, no reflash between trials): vel_kp 0.0014->0.0016, vel_kff 0.00135->0.0008. History: the ORIGINAL 0.0018 loop had a ~140 mm/s overshoot RESONANCE (+24..+33% on a velocity step); the 2026-07-12 interim detune (vel_kp 0.0018->0.0014, vel_ki 0.008->0.005, vel_kaw 15->20) only halved it (~+11%, still over the <~10% bar) and cost rise time. This session's own bench grid at kp=0.0014/kff=0.00135 measured worst-case +25% at 140mm/s (reproducing the historical pattern -- the interim detune alone did not clear the bar this session either). Root cause, found by exhausting kp/ki/kff/iMax/kaw per architecture-update.md (106) Decision 4: kff (feedforward) was OVER-estimated -- raising it (tried 0.0016) made overshoot WORSE (kff*target is an immediate open-loop kick added on top of kp*error, so an over-large kff over-drives the plant right at the step) -- confirming the 2026-07-11 kff derivation's own flagged 620-740mm/s measurement variance was real drift, not noise. Lowering kff to 0.0008 (with kp still at 0.0014) killed the resonance (worst 2.1%) but slowed rise time by ~30-50% (0.9-1.5s vs the interim's 0.9-1.28s) -- kp=0.0016 restores it: 3 consecutive full-grid confirmation runs all passed the <~10% bar with FASTER rise times than the interim detune (worst overshoot 9.3%/4.3%/5.0%; rise times 0.28-0.98s vs the interim's 0.9-1.5s) -- both overshoot AND rise time improved over the shipped interim, not just traded off. vel_ki/vel_kaw unchanged (0.005/20.0) -- the fix lived entirely in kp/kff, ki/kaw were not the lever needed this time. Re-verified from a clean reflash (boot defaults only, no live config() call) after persisting -- see 106-002's own completion notes for the full before/after table. Endpoint-accuracy re-verification (turn_sweep.py-style angle grid) NOT re-run this session -- flagged as a follow-up if endpoint regressions are observed, per the interim detune's own precedent of trading a little endpoint accuracy for trajectory smoothness. vel_filt=0.3 unchanged. See clasi/sprints/106-host-trajectory-planner-profiled-twists-straights-and-turns/issues/heading-loop-output-clamp-and-velocity-resonance.md's own Part 2 (marked resolved by 106-002) for the fuller history.

control._drive_calibration_note: 2026-08-01 (130-001, population duty-sweep protocol): duty_sweep.py extended to the FULL duty range (0.04-1.0, was 0.04-0.60), per motor per direction, plus a simultaneous-both-wheels grid and a --from-csv refit path -- see the script's own header for the full protocol. Two corrections found and fixed in the tool itself: (1) it was inverting the duty axis off THIS file's duty_per_speed_left/right, which boot_calibration.cpp has ignored since 2026-07-31 (Drive::kDutyPerSpeed is now baked in firmware, config-independent) -- the tool now hardcodes the firmware's actual constant (0.001182) instead, cross-checked every run by a constant-free saturation reading; (2) the default fit window's upper bound (0.28, picked before this session's own full-range data existed) was too narrow, spanning only 3 near-breakaway rungs -- the LEFT wheel's complete curve (both directions, full range) shows genuinely linear behavior with a STEADY local slope of ~1000-1200 mm/s per duty all the way to duty~0.55 (NOT ~0.30 as 129-006 estimated from a 0.60-ceiling sweep), then a sharp one-rung collapse into saturation (peak 584 mm/s fwd @ duty 0.596 / 555 rev @ duty 0.545; 570/521 mm/s at full duty, only -2 to -6% off peak) -- 129-006's saturation-onset estimate was itself session-specific, not a fixed ceiling; the tool's default fit-duty-max is now 0.50. Refit over [0.12,0.50]: left fwd 1101.3 mm/s/duty (offset -14.2), left rev 1023.1 (offset +1.7) -- this SUPERSEDES the 129-006/06-issue figure of L 853.6 for the left wheel (that fit's 0.12-0.60 window, with no upper cutoff, blended the genuinely-linear region with the very onset of saturation at its top edge, biasing the slope down). SESSION FAULT, INCOMPLETE RIGHT WHEEL: the robot went hard-silent (no PING, no telemetry) after 45 good rungs, right-fwd duty=0.293 onward -- confirmed via read-only pyOCD halt+backtrace (core running, PC in RAM, spinning in codal::system_timer_wait_cycles/system_timer_current_time) and reproduced across 2 fresh reconnects including a hard DTR reset; matches the documented dead-motor-brick-battery/unpowered-external-I2C-bus signature (banner+frames then total silence, every reboot re-wedges), NOT a cable/USB-enumeration issue (mbdeploy list stayed healthy). Right wheel therefore has only 3 usable fwd rungs (duty<=0.242, fit gain 1197.8 mm/s/duty, LOW CONFIDENCE -- not re-verified against its own full range) and ZERO reverse or simultaneous-grid data this session; the OLD 129-006 R 837.8 figure is UNCONFIRMED, not superseded, pending completion. The parallel-lines/population verdict computed from this incomplete n=3 sample came out slope-dominated (fanned) -- OPPOSITE the stakeholder's intercept-only hypothesis -- but is flagged LOW CONFIDENCE for the same reason (the right-wheel line rests on 3 near-breakaway points) and must not be treated as settling Stage C's design question either way. Derived (report-only, NOT applied to any config key): biasMax +-23.8 mm/s (offset population envelope), vMin 99.7 mm/s (worst breakaway duty 0.09 x mean gain), breakaway band 0.04-0.09 duty (44-100 mm/s); candidate Stage-A wheel_gain/intercept-decel values per wheel/direction were also computed but, per this file's own _wheel_correction_note below, are NOT written here -- refitting that pair from bench/encoder data is exactly what that note warns against; camera-measured verification is still required first. Battery was NOT freshly charged or independently verified before this session (the robot has no pack-voltage telemetry, so charge state can only be inferred, not measured) -- given the session ended in a hard fault matching the known dead-battery/unpowered-bus signature, this raises 129-006's own flagged battery-artifact possibility from a soft caveat to the leading hypothesis for tonight's failure specifically (separate from, and not proof of, 129-006's ORIGINAL saturation/decline finding, which this session's own data already partially supersedes for the left wheel). The full population campaign (physically swapping motors) and a freshly-charged-battery re-run are BOTH deferred to the same stakeholder-scheduled follow-on bench session, which must ALSO complete the right wheel's full range and the simultaneous grid before any of tonight's derived constants should be trusted as final. Prior note follows, superseded where noted above: duty_per_speed_* [duty/(mm/s)]: open-loop wheel calibration, the inverse of the measured plant gain (speed_sweep 2026-07-27: L ~560, R ~510 mm/s per duty; ceiling ~500 mm/s). Per-wheel because the two gearboxes differ ~10%. crawl_pulse [-1,1]: fixed pulse amplitude for sub-breakaway wheel speeds, Bresenham-dithered in App::Drive; 0 disables. Measured breakaway is 1-6% duty and state-dependent (src/tests/firmware/duty_min/RESULTS.md) -- the earlier 0.20 was sized against a duty_sweep criterion that the standalone prober disproved, so crawl ships OFF pending a re-measure of the low end.
control._wheel_correction_note: IDENTITY as of 2026-07-31 (stakeholder). The fitted values (tovez: gain ~1.47) were measured against a duty_per_speed that was itself wrong by ~1.6x, so the pair was circularly calibrated -- each fitted against the other's error -- and the correction ended up pointing the WRONG WAY: it divided a 150mm/s request down to 96 before the duty conversion, on a robot that was already under-delivering. duty_per_speed is now a baked measured constant (App::Drive::kDutyPerSpeed), so this affine stage has nothing left to correct and is held at identity. Separately: this session's saturation reading (L 571.7/R 532.5mm/s at full duty) and residual-sweep percentages both measure LOWER than ab303ee3's own 2026-07-31 baseline (L 760-795/R 696 saturation; ~94-99%/70-86% residual) -- an unexplained ~20-25% apparent plant-gain drop since that measurement, flagged but NOT root-caused this session (no pack-voltage telemetry to confirm or rule out a battery-state difference between sessions). Plant ID 2026-07-26 (square_tour_sim.py tourLimits() / on-robot tour): gain ~1370 mm/s per duty, tau ~230 ms. NOT the retired control.vel_*/a_max/... blocks above -- those fed the deleted NezhaMotor MotorVelocityPid and Motion::VelocityShaper (itself also since deleted); deployed as-is against THIS controller (kp 0.0016, aMax 800, jMax 5000) they limit-cycled the real wheels at ~2-3 Hz across the whole first on-robot tour (2026-07-27 plot) -- this block is what supersedes them for Motion::Planner specifically.
planner._timing_note: control_period/actuation_delay: UPDATED 130-007 (one 50ms control period everywhere) -- App::RobotLoop::kCycle raised 40->50ms specifically so the pacer fits the loop's own measured busy time (~21ms) and paces exactly, closing the gap this note used to describe (the OLD 47ms value was the MEASURED delivered period at kCycle=40, ~7ms of vendor-bus-clearance overrun the 40ms nominal did not include -- three dishonest numbers for one physical quantity). At kCycle=50 the delivered period IS the nominal, stable, so control_period/actuation_delay now simply equal kCycle rather than a separately-measured value. The planner's discrete math (accel steps, braking sums, ramp tick counts) must still use the period the loop actually delivers; telemetry cycle_period re-measures this on every frame if the schedule ever changes.
planner._settle_note: require_settle OFF (stakeholder 2026-07-27): the creep/breakaway-kick landing machinery pulsed the wheels at ~0.18 duty against gearbox stiction after every move -- functional but unacceptable sawtooth. Landing residual (small at the measured 47ms period) is instead absorbed by the NEXT chained move via the cumulative baseline ledger, at full speed where the plant is linear and no stiction compensation is needed. settle_rest_velocity/settle_rest_omega are sized to the measured hardware encoder-velocity noise (plant ID 2026-07-26: ~+-7mm/s at rest) -- the rest-damping stage outputs exactly zero duty below the floor, so it must clear the noise band or the wheels twitch at rest forever. settle_epsilon_linear/settle_epsilon_angular are arrival tolerances sized to the stiction-limited creep resolution (one duty_floor pulse per period ~= 2-4deg of heading): tighter is unreachable and just burns settle_window at every landing -- the demonstrated one-sided-creep resolution (single-turn probe 2026-07-27 landed +1.76deg; the right wheel does not reverse under the breakaway kick, so fine correction rides the left wheel). heading_hold_gain is sim-validated.
planner._duty_stage_note: duty_floor (stiction floor): must clear the gearbox BREAKAWAY duty, not merely MotorArmor's write-suppression threshold (output_deadband 0.03 above -- a whine gate, not a friction model). 0.18 is estimated from the measured integral wind-up time to first motion during the stalled settle creep (2026-07-27 single-turn trace); replace with a proper plant-ID breakaway measurement when one exists. vel_kp/vel_ki/vel_i_max/vel_i_accel_gate are the measured-plant duty-stage gains (square_tour_sim.py tourLimits()); vel_kff/vel_kaff are DERIVED by gen_boot_config.py from plant_gain/plant_tau (kff=1/gain, kaff=tau/gain -- physics-derived), not stored here.
planner._trim_note: VELOCITY-DOMAIN TRIM (wheel_trim.h) -- the closed loop that actually reaches the wheels. trim_kp is DIMENSIONLESS (mm/s of trim per mm/s of error): the sim tour ran 0.25 against a +-4.8% wheel mismatch; this robot's residual after the 2026-07-27 calibration is ~2%, and measured wheel velocity is a raw per-tick difference quotient, so it starts at 0.15 -- COMMISSIONING VALUE, to be raised on the stand rather than trusted. An over-gained loop on THIS hardware limit-cycled at 2-3Hz (see _domain_note above) -- the failure to watch for. trim_kaff is DERIVED (plant_tau/2, not stored here): the FULL plant tau measured UNSTABLE in sim (closure 696mm vs 16mm at half) -- half it is. decel_plan_fraction plans the brake START at 40% of the decel ceiling, keeping the rest in reserve so the plant can TRACK the ramp down and arrive at each boundary already slow instead of coasting past (tau ~230ms) -- swept 0.0-0.6 in sim, 0.4 gave the best closure (16.0 vs 23.3mm).
